description: We are a team of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering students interested in space technology, prototyping, optimization, and AI. Our strengths include CAD, system design, 3D printing, analysis, and developing practical engineering solutions.
summary:
ASTRASHIELD is an interactive, AI-assisted fire-safety research platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research more accessible and understandable.

Our project combines a web-based research dashboard with a 3D-printed spacecraft habitat controlled by an Arduino Mega 2560. Users adjust five simulation parameters to explore different scenarios, visualize illustrative flame behavior, and compare their selected conditions with NASA's experimental findings.

Using research from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics database, ASTRASHIELD examines experimental similarities, identifies relevant combustion investigations, and highlights limitations in the available evidence. Three confidence indicators distinguish strong, partial, and insufficient experimental support, while additional LEDs and a buzzer enhance the physical demonstration.

Rather than generating unsupported fire-risk predictions, ASTRASHIELD emphasizes scientific transparency and identifies areas requiring further investigation.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex scientific research and practical understanding, supporting education, future research, and the development of safer space habitats.
details:
The Problem

Fire presents a serious challenge during human space exploration. In microgravity, the absence of ordinary buoyancy-driven convection changes flame behavior, while factors such as oxygen concentration, airflow, and material properties influence combustion.

NASA has conducted numerous experiments to investigate these phenomena. However, the findings are distributed across different investigations, experimental configurations, and data formats, making them difficult to compare and interpret.

Our Solution

ASTRASHIELD addresses this challenge through an interactive research dashboard connected to a physical spacecraft-habitat demonstrator.

Our platform allows users to explore simulated environmental conditions and identify relevant NASA combustion experiments. By comparing experimental parameters, the system helps users understand which findings are applicable to a selected scenario and where additional evidence is needed.

NASA Data and AI Integration

The project draws on NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics repository, including investigations such as BASS-II, Saffire-I, SAME, SAME-R, FLEX, and BASS Modeling.

These studies address different aspects of spacecraft fire safety, including flame propagation, large-scale fire growth, smoke detection, fire extinction, and numerical combustion modeling.

Our computational approach uses experimental-data organization, similarity-based retrieval, and exploratory machine-learning techniques to support the comparison and interpretation of research findings.

The platform distinguishes documented experimental results from illustrative simulations and identifies cases in which the available evidence is insufficient.

Physical Demonstration

ASTRASHIELD includes a custom-designed, 3D-printed spacecraft habitat integrated with an Arduino Mega 2560.

The physical prototype incorporates five potentiometers, a TFT display, three confidence LEDs, six additional habitat LEDs controlled through one PWM signal, and a buzzer.

The confidence LEDs communicate the strength of the available experimental evidence:

Green indicates strong experimental support, yellow indicates partial support, and red indicates insufficient evidence.

The additional LEDs and buzzer support the illustrative fire-simulation demonstration. These outputs do not represent an actual fire-detection system.

Software and Technologies

The project combines Arduino C++, Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, alongside data-processing and machine-learning tools.

The interactive interface provides experimental comparisons, visualizations, and explanations intended to make NASA's combustion research easier to explore.

Innovation and Impact

ASTRASHIELD combines scientific research, artificial intelligence, electronics, and physical prototyping into a single interactive educational platform.

Its main contribution is not simply displaying combustion data, but helping users understand the relationship between experimental conditions, available evidence, and scientific uncertainty.

The project is intended to support students, researchers, educators, and early-stage spacecraft designers by making fire-safety research more accessible.

Future improvements could include expanding the verified experimental database, refining evidence classification, and validating numerical predictions when suitable data become available.

Ultimately, ASTRASHIELD aims to contribute to safer future space exploration by highlighting both what NASA has already established and what remains to be investigated.
